t.3.54.1: Bṛhadaśva said: Then, when the auspicious time had arrived, on a holy lunar day and at a propitious moment, King Bhīma summoned the lords of the earth to the svayaṃvara.
t.3.54.2: Hearing that, all the kings, tormented by love, came together in haste, desiring Damayantī.
t.3.54.3: Those kings entered the great arena, beautiful with its golden pillars and resplendent with its arched gateway, as lions enter a mountain.
t.3.54.4: There, seated upon thrones of various kinds, were the lords of the earth, all wearing fragrant garlands and earrings of well-polished jewels.
t.3.54.5: That assembly of kings, full as Bhogavatī is full of Nāgas, and thronged with tigers among men as a mountain cave is thronged with tigers…
t.3.54.6: There were seen thick arms like iron bars, well-shaped and very smooth, like five-headed serpents.
t.3.54.7: The faces of the kings, lovely and auspicious, framed by fine locks of hair and graced with shapely noses, shone like the stars in the sky.
t.3.54.8: Then the fair-faced Damayantī entered the arena, stealing with her radiance both the eyes and the hearts of the kings.
t.3.54.9: The gaze of those great-souled ones, falling upon her limbs, became fixed wherever it fell, and it did not move as they looked on.
t.3.54.10: Then, O Bhārata, as the names of the kings were being proclaimed, Bhaimī saw five men who seemed alike in form.
t.3.54.11: Then, gazing upon all of them standing there with forms in no way different, the princess of Vidarbha, out of doubt, could not recognize King Nala. For whichever one of them she looked at, that one she took to be King Nala.
t.3.54.12: Then the beautiful lady, pondering with her mind, reflected: "How indeed may I recognize the gods? How may I know King Nala?"
t.3.54.13: Reflecting thus, the princess of Vidarbha, deeply distressed, called to mind the marks of the gods that she had heard of, O Bhārata.
t.3.54.14: The marks of the gods that I have heard of from the elders, I do not perceive here in even a single one of those standing upon the ground.
t.3.54.15: Having deliberated in many ways and reflected again and again, she judged that the time had come to seek refuge with the gods.
t.3.54.16: Having offered homage to the gods with both speech and mind, she joined her palms in reverence and, trembling, spoke these words.
t.3.54.17: As truly as, having heard the words of the swans, I chose the Naiṣadha as my husband, by that truth may the gods reveal him to me.
t.3.54.18: As surely as I do not transgress against him in word or even in thought, by that truth may the gods point him out to me.
t.3.54.19: As the lord of the Niṣadhas has been ordained by the gods to be my husband, by that truth may the gods point out that very one to me.
t.3.54.20: May the guardians of the worlds, together with their lords, assume their own true form, so that I may recognize the king of men, Puṇyaśloka, of holy fame.
t.3.54.21: Having heard that piteous lament of Damayantī, her supreme and true resolve, and her deep love for the Naiṣadha,
t.3.54.24: The Naiṣadha, casting a shadow, his garland withered, covered with dust and sweat, standing upon the ground, was also revealed by the blinking of his eyes.
t.3.54.23: She saw all the gods: they were free of sweat, their eyes did not blink, their garlands were fresh and free of dust, and they stood without touching the ground.
t.3.54.22: Seeing her purity of mind and her understanding, her devotion and her love, O Bhārata, the gods did just as she had asked and used their power to bear their distinguishing marks.
t.3.54.25: Then, O Bhārata, having looked upon the gods and upon the one of holy fame, Bhaimī chose the Naiṣadha in accordance with dharma, O Bhārata.
t.3.54.26: Blushing with shame, the large-eyed one took hold of the hem of his garment, and upon his shoulder she placed a most beautiful garland; and thus the fair-complexioned lady chose him for her husband.
t.3.54.27: Then the kings suddenly let out a cry of "Alas, alas!" while the gods and great seers, O Bhārata, filled with wonder and praising King Nala, raised the cry, "Well done, well done!"
t.3.54.28: When the Naiṣadha had been chosen by Bhaimī, the mighty guardians of the world, all delighted at heart, gave Nala eight boons.
t.3.54.29: Śakra, the lord of Śacī, being pleased, granted to the Naiṣadha a visible manifestation of himself at the sacrifice and a supreme, auspicious destiny.
t.3.54.30: Agni granted that he himself would appear wherever the Naiṣadha wished, and Hutāśana also gave him worlds radiant with his own splendor.
t.3.54.31: Yama gave the savour of food and the highest steadfastness in dharma; the lord of the waters gave the presence of water wherever the Naiṣadha should wish it.
t.3.54.32: And a garland rich with the finest fragrance; and all of them together gave a pair. Having thus bestowed boons upon him, those gods went to the threefold heaven.
t.3.54.33: And the kings, having witnessed the wedding of this Damayantī, filled with wonder and delighted, returned as they had come.
t.3.54.34: Having won that jewel among women, the king too, the lord of the earth of holy renown, delighted in her company, as the slayer of Bala and Vṛtra delighted with Śacī.
t.3.54.35: Exceedingly delighted, the king, shining like the radiant sun, the hero, gladdened his subjects, protecting them in accordance with dharma.
t.3.54.37: And again Nala, like an immortal, took his pleasure with Damayantī in delightful forests and groves.
t.3.54.36: And like Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, the wise one also sacrificed with the Aśvamedha and with many other rites accompanied by ample sacrificial fees.
t.3.54.38: Thus, sacrificing and taking his pleasure, that lord of men, the sovereign of the earth, protected the earth, which was filled with wealth.
